The text explores the tension between societal expectations and personal desires in *Pride and Prejudice*, highlighting how different reader backgrounds shape their interpretation. Feminist readers may view Elizabeth Bennet as a symbol of female agency and independence, celebrating her resistance to conforming to restrictive gender roles. In contrast, traditionalist readers might emphasize the validity of social standing, family reputation, and the structural realities of the time, viewing these elements as essential components of stability and order. This duality illustrates how literature can serve as a mirror for diverse values, allowing readers to project their own cultural and ideological frameworks onto the narrative.

The primary use of a bed is for sleeping.
